newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel, PLO set for clash over Jerusalem.
newsitem.headline: Israel, PLO set for clash over Jerusalem.

text.p: The threat of violence loomed large as Israel was set on Wednesday to approve construction of a new Jewish neighbourhood in Arab East Jerusalem.
Palestinians said the plan would grind peace moves to a halt and warned of clashes. In one West Bank village, violence had already begun.
Israeli undercover soldiers killed a Palestinian and wounded three others in Hizmeh north of Jerusalem on Tuesday after being cornered by stone-throwers, the army said.
"The force responded with fire, killing one Palestinian, wounding one moderately to severely and wounding two others lightly," an army spokesman said.

Palestinians said the soldiers, dressed in civilian clothes, provoked residents of the village. Palestinian President Yasser Arafat's aide described death of a 56-year-old Palestinian in the shooting as a crime.
"This is a crime that has been carried out by the secret units which continue to function as if there are no agreements or political negotiations," said Ahmed Tibi.

The violence exacerbated tensions ahead of a meeting on Wednesday at 2.30 p.m. (1230 GMT) in which Israeli cabinet ministers were expected to approve construction of a new Jewish neighbourhood in Arab East Jerusalem.

Earlier on Tuesday Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu appealed to Palestinians not to react violently when he gives the green light to build 6,500 homes for Jews on Har Homa, called Jabal Abu Ghneim by Arabs, a tree-covered hill taken by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war.
"Whoever wants the peace process to continue will understand that violence will achieve nothing," Netanyahu told reporters in parliament.
"I want to clarify unequivocally: we will build in all Jerusalem. We will also build at Har Homa."
The PLO said that the decision would wreck the peace process.

"Netanyahu's statements torpedo the whole peace process. This is a violation of the peace accord and he has to pay the price for such measures," Arafat's aide Nabil Abu Radaineh told Reuters by phone from Morocco.

Palestinians and Israeli leftists have warned the plan would ignite Arab rage reminiscent of September clashes sparked by Netanyahu's opening of an entrance to a tunnel near Moslem holy sites in Jerusalem. Sixty-one Arabs and 15 Israelis were killed.

Some 150 Palestinian demonstrators marched towards Jabal Abu Ghneim from self-ruled Bethlehem in the West Bank on Tuesday to protest against the plan but they were prevented by Israeli police from reaching Jerusalem, witnesses said.
"We are telling them (Israel): you are playing with fire," Faisal al-Husseini, the top Palestinian Authority official in Jerusalem, told reporters. "There will be an explosion."
Israel handed over parts of the West Bank to Palestinian rule under peace deals signed since 1993 but Israeli soldiers still patrol other areas of the West Bank.

The two sides left the status of Jerusalem, one of the most sensitive issues in the Arab-Israel conflict, for talks on the final status of the West Bank and Gaza Strip which must be completed by 1999.
Israel claims all of the city as its capital. Palestinians view East Jerusalem as the capital of their future state.
